parsedVerdict.reasoning: The unit passes. Both files deal with one thing: the admin queue-management HTTP endpoints. queue.module.ts connects QueueController to QueueService and imports the three queue modules that QueueService depends on. QueueController exposes four job endpoints (list, delete-many, delete-one, execute). Each one only hands the work to QueueService, so the controller never goes around the service to reach the bull queues directly. Every handler uses the same access check (HasPermission(permissions.accessAdminControl) plus AuthGuard('jwt') and HasPermissionGuard). Repeating these decorators on each method is normal NestJS practice and doesn't move a rule out of its one home: the permission rule itself still lives in the shared guard and decorator. There is one small repeat. The status-filter parsing (`filterByStatus?.split(',') as JobStatus[]`) appears in both deleteJobs and getJobs. It's a minor input-parsing helper rather than a domain rule or invariant, so it doesn't amount to a cohesion failure. It could be pulled into a pipe or helper.
